routes.label: Recognize a square in the coefficients

question:
If

\[ \begin{aligned} (7+4\sqrt3)x^2 &+(2+\sqrt3)x\\ &-2=0, \end{aligned} \]

the larger root minus the smaller root is:
solution:
The leading coefficient is the square of the linear coefficient:
\[
(2+\sqrt3)^2=7+4\sqrt3.
\]
Let \(u=2+\sqrt3\), so \(u>0\). Treating \(ux\) as one quantity turns the equation into
\[
(ux)^2+ux-2=0,
\qquad (ux-1)(ux+2)=0.
\]
Because \(u\ne0\), the two roots are \(\frac1u\) and \(-\frac2u\). The first is larger since \(u>0\), so their difference is
\[
\frac1u-\left(-\frac2u\right)
=\frac3{2+\sqrt3}
=\frac{3(2-\sqrt3)}{4-3}
=6-3\sqrt3.
\]
Therefore the answer is choice D.
